Top candidates: Anthracnose, Phomopsis, Diaporthe, Charcoal_Rot. Let me view reference images.

Anthracnose shows dark lesions on pods closely matching the test image. Phomopsis shows more circular pycnidial patterns. Diaporthe and Charcoal_Rot are mainly stem diseases. Let me check a few more for completeness.

None of those match. Purple_Seed_Stain shows seed discoloration, Septoria/Cercospora are leaf diseases, Fusarium is root/stem. Anthracnose remains top candidate. Let me view more references to meet the 12-image minimum.

I've now viewed 13 reference images. All other candidates (White_Mold = white mycelium on stems, Frogeye = leaf spots, Soybean_rust = leaf pustules, Brown_Stem_Rot = internal stem browning) do not match the pod symptoms in the test image.

**Analysis summary:**
- **Test image**: A soybean pod held in hand, tan/cream-colored with hairy texture, showing concentrated dark brown/black lesions in the middle section of the pod
- **Anthracnose** reference (bottom-left quadrant): Shows an identical presentation — hairy tan pod with dark brown/black irregular lesions — this is the best match
- **Phomopsis**: Shows circular pycnidial ring patterns on pods, more uniform tan-brown discoloration — different from the concentrated dark lesions in the test image
- All stem/root/leaf diseases (Diaporthe, Charcoal_Rot, Fusarium, Brown_Stem_Rot, etc.) are ruled out since the test image shows pod symptoms
